title: Inject an OS file picker into a service
summary: A service asks for the operating system's file picker by injection. `tac.nativeCapabilities: ["filePicker"]` in `client/manifest.json` grants it, separately from `tac.browserApis`. Without the grant, every call answers `denied` before a panel opens. The grant does not replace the user's choice or the signing entitlements: a sandboxed macOS app also needs the user-selected read-only file entitlement, and Tachyon does not add it for you. `open` lets the user choose one file; the only type filters are `text/plain` and `application/json`, and an empty list allows any file. The answer holds the file name and an opaque handle, never a path. `readText(handle)` reads at most 65,536 bytes of UTF-8 text, and `release(handle)` ends access. A handle belongs to the service that asked for it. It ends after 300 seconds, or sooner when that service goes away. Every answer is a typed status (`selected`, `cancelled`, `read`, `released`, `denied`, `unsupported`, `unavailable`, `invalid`, `disposed` or `tooLarge`); nothing throws. The picker opens a panel (NSOpenPanel) only on macOS, for JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust and Swift services (ADR 0089). A browser tab and the iOS, Android, Linux and Windows apps open no panel and answer `unsupported`. JavaScript and TypeScript inject `filePicker` with `@Needs` and get Promises. Rust declares a `FilePicker` field in a `Default` service, so the same file builds for every target. Swift and C# ask for an uninitialized `FilePicker` field with `NeedsAll`, but only in an app that links the service: Swift on macOS and iOS, and C# on Windows, where it answers `unsupported` because Windows has no picker yet. A Swift or C# service that runs as WebAssembly cannot ask for a FilePicker yet, and the build stops with `TY1407`. So their files are under native/ here; put the one for your target in client/services. A Kotlin service cannot ask for a FilePicker yet on any target: the build stops with `TY1405`. Dart, Go, Ruby, Java, F#, Lua and Python services always run in the page and have no FilePicker type, so this feature has no tab for them. Let a JavaScript, TypeScript or Rust service use the picker and send the text to them with an event.
